proposal_source: Blackbox Log BBL-2026-09-07-217 (founder ruling, Blackbox Log record 10.5281/zenodo.22302518) -- Core Epistemic Structure of a project, applied first in The Economics of Expertise in the Age of Generative AI v1.0.1 (Zenodo record 22636999, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22636999)
extractor_note: TOLEDO REGISTRAR pass over founder ruling Blackbox Log BBL-2026-09-07-217, which defines the Core Epistemic Structure of a project p as [New Definition / Proposal]: (i) E_p = <X_p^exp, X_p^int, M_p^AI>; (ii) M_p^AI = {M_1,...,M_k}; (iii) X_p^int = empty-set when no interactional expert holds the role (an unheld role, not a zero score); (iv) the non-collapse rule Experience-Based Expertise != Interactional Expertise != AI Model; (v) the experience-holder decomposition X_p^exp = <Exp, Sel, Int> (lived experience, selection, interpretation), from BBL-2026-09-07 rulings the same day. Five distinct CANONICAL objects are proposed, one per sub-definition (aliases CES:E_p, CES:M_AI, CES:X_int_empty, CES:non-collapse, CES:X_exp), because (iv) is tiered Dr (an asserted non-collapse rule, not a bare typed definition) while (i),(ii),(iii),(v) are tiered Definition -- a single CANONICAL entry carries exactly one tier field, so the five cannot be merged into one object. All five read/refine the two Task-1-assigned Economics-of-Expertise readings that state the same registration architecture in the manuscript's own numbering (weld/H.22.v1 Eq.4 'credential != expertise', weld/H.23.v1 Eq.5 'project role != expertise type != AI system') and the registration object itself (weld/H.28.v1, Eq.11-13, the Core Epistemic Registration object R_p = <E_p^exp, E_p^int, M_p^AI>) -- this ruling's E_p/X_p^exp/X_p^int/M_p^AI notation refines that same registration architecture into its own named structure and decomposition. This file is NEW ORIGINAL CONTENT transcribed from the cited Blackbox Log ruling -- none of it is copied from CANONICAL.json, genesis_root.json, LINEAGE.jsonl, coq/, latex/, or mcp/, and none of those were edited.

proposals.name: Core Epistemic Structure of a project

parents.evidence: Eq.(4) 'credential != expertise' is the load-bearing non-collapse the Core Epistemic Structure keeps distinct across its three components.
Eq.(5) 'project role != expertise type != AI system' is the exact three-way non-collapse E_p's three components (X_p^exp, X_p^int, M_p^AI) formalize as a named structure.

Refines the Core Epistemic Registration object R_p = <E_p^exp, E_p^int, M_p^AI> (Eq.11-13) into the founder-ruled Core Epistemic Structure notation E_p = <X_p^exp, X_p^int, M_p^AI> of BBL-2026-09-07-217.

proposals.name: Interactional-expert slot empty when the role is unheld

statement.latest: X_p^{int} = \varnothing \quad \text{(role unheld, not a zero score)}

parents.evidence: Eq.(4) 'credential != expertise' underlies why an unheld interactional-expert role must be recorded as an empty slot rather than credentialed-but-scored-zero.
Eq.(5) 'project role != expertise type != AI system' licenses a role (interactional expert) being genuinely absent from a project without that absence collapsing into another category.

Refines the E_p^int component of the Core Epistemic Registration object R_p (Eq.11-13, itself Eq.12: 'empty set if none present') into its own standalone CANONICAL reading, naming explicitly that an unheld role is not a zero score.

proposals.name: Non-collapse: experience-based expertise, interactional expertise, and AI model are distinct

parents.evidence: Eq.(4) 'credential != expertise' is the same-shaped non-collapse this rule generalizes from a two-term to a three-term chain.

Eq.(5) 'project role != expertise type != AI system' is the three-way non-collapse this rule restates in the Core Epistemic Structure's own vocabulary (Experience-Based Expertise, Interactional Expertise, AI Model in place of project role, expertise type, AI system).
Refines the three non-collapsing components of the Core Epistemic Registration object R_p (Eq.11-13) into an explicit asserted non-collapse rule over those same three components.
